headline: Attackers exploit a PaperCut print-server zero-day as ServiceNow, cPanel, and Gitea scramble to patch critical remote-code-execution flaws across enterprise software.

emerging_trends.text: Print servers, IT-service platforms, and hosting panels all sprang critical leaks at once, and PaperCut's actively exploited zero-day forced an emergency patch across every NG and MF version.
emerging_trends.topic_title: PaperCut Print Server Zero-Day Under Active Attack

emerging_trends.text: Washington moved to bar foreign-made power-grid components the same week VulnCheck exposed factory root implants in Chinese ZBT routers, sharpening fears that hardware supply chains carry hidden backdoors.
emerging_trends.topic_title: White House Bans Foreign-Made Power Grid Equipment

emerging_trends.text: Federal prosecutors charged two men behind TeamPCP's Shai-Hulud worm, which self-propagated through software supply chains to hit more than 1,000 organizations and steal 500,000 credentials.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Two Charged Over TeamPCP's Shai-Hulud Supply-Chain Worm

topics.title: Critical RCE Flaws Hit ServiceNow, cPanel, and Gitea
topics.latest_developments: ServiceNow patched three CVSS 10.0 AI Platform flaws that unauthenticated attackers can exploit for code injection, SQL injection, and privilege escalation, cPanel fixed root-level CVE-2026-65643 across all supported cPanel and WHM versions, and Shadowserver counted over 8,300 Gitea servers still exposed to the actively exploited code-injection flaw CVE-2026-60004.
topics.summary: The flaws span three widely deployed platforms: ServiceNow's AI Platform, cPanel and WHM hosting control, and self-hosted Gitea code repositories. Organizations should patch immediately, since attackers already hit Gitea in the wild.

sources.title: Three CVSS 10.0 ServiceNow Flaws Could Let Unauthenticated Attackers Execute Code and SQL
ServiceNow warns of three max severity security vulnerabilities
Critical cPanel Flaw Could Let One Hosting Customer Take Root Control of a Whole Server
Over 8,300 Gitea servers vulnerable to code execution attacks

topics.title: PaperCut Print Server Zero-Day Under Active Attack
topics.latest_developments: PaperCut issued an emergency advisory Thursday evening and shipped patches for v25 and v26 after confirming attackers actively exploit an as-yet-unassigned flaw across all NG and MF versions, citing confirmed customer incidents it treats as top priority.
topics.summary: PaperCut NG and MF run print management for enterprises worldwide. Administrators should install the emergency v25 or v26 patch and apply the recommended mitigations at once.

sources.title: PaperCut warns of hackers using printer management software flaw in attacks
PaperCut Releases Emergency Patch for Exploited Zero-Day
PaperCut Zero-Day Exploited in Attacks, Affecting All NG and MF Versions

topics.title: White House Bans Foreign-Made Power Grid Equipment
topics.latest_developments: The Trump administration barred acquisition of foreign-made components used to manage electricity and power generation, alleging that certain foreign actors increasingly create and exploit vulnerabilities in the technology, days after VulnCheck disclosed factory root implants in Chinese-built ZBT routers.
topics.summary: The order blocks federal acquisition of foreign-made electricity-management components on grounds that adversaries plant and exploit vulnerabilities in them. It lands amid fresh disclosures of built-in backdoors in Chinese hardware.

sources.title: White House bans foreign-made equipment for power generation over cyber backdoor concerns
Chinese Routers Sold Worldwide Contain Backdoors
China-Made ZBT Routers Ship With Two Implants Giving Unauthenticated Attackers Root Access

topics.title: Two Charged Over TeamPCP's Shai-Hulud Supply-Chain Worm
topics.latest_developments: Authorities arrested and charged two alleged members of TeamPCP over the self-propagating Shai-Hulud worm that infected more than 1,000 organizations, including OpenAI, and harvested roughly 500,000 credentials in a relentless supply-chain campaign.
topics.summary: TeamPCP, whose worm carries the name of a Dune sandworm, spread on its own through software dependencies to steal credentials at scale. The charges mark a major law-enforcement strike against the crew.

sources.title: Authorities arrest 2 alleged members of prolific hacking group TeamPCP
Shai-Hulud hackers: two men charged over TeamPCP's global supply chain crime spree that hit OpenAI, and thousands more

topics.title: Flock License-Plate Network Sprawls Across Thousands of Agencies
topics.latest_developments: Wired revealed that Alpharetta, Georgia police share Flock automated license-plate data with more than 2,000 organizations ranging from federal agencies to a fish and wildlife commission, and separately documented a Georgia officer who used Flock to track his ex-partner and a man whose vehicle often appeared near hers.
topics.summary: Flock's automated license-plate readers feed a sharing network that now reaches thousands of public and private entities. The Georgia cases show how readily officers can abuse the data for personal ends.

sources.title: How an Atlanta Suburb Ended Up Sharing Flock Data With More Than 2,000 Organizations
A Georgia Cop Used Flock to Track 2 Other Cops: His Ex and Her Friend

topics.title: APT28 Deploys HOOKEDGE Backdoor on European Governments
topics.latest_developments: Recorded Future's Insikt Group tied the previously undocumented HOOKEDGE backdoor, a lightweight Windows batch script, to APT28 campaigns that hit government and diplomatic organizations in Romania, Spain, and Türkiye between late September 2025 and early April 2026.
topics.summary: APT28, the Russian military-intelligence group, distributed HOOKEDGE through crafted lures against diplomats. Targeted organizations should hunt for the batch-script backdoor and inspect email-borne delivery.

sources.title: APT28-Linked HOOKEDGE Backdoor Targets European Government and Diplomatic Organizations
